items: Compare pendant shapes at a glance
Solitaire pendants: one diamond in focus
Geometric pendants: defined lines and structure
How to choose the right pendant shape

content.text: A solitaire pendant puts the focus on one centre diamond. A circle pendant creates a rounded, continuous silhouette; a star pendant adds a recognisable symbolic shape; a floral pendant uses petal-like details; and a geometric pendant has a more structured, modern outline. Choose by the shape you want people to notice and the style you will wear often.

content.heading: Solitaire pendants: one diamond in focus

content.text: A solitaire pendant centres the design on one diamond. Its clean silhouette makes the stone the main detail, without a larger outline or multiple decorative elements competing for attention.

Choose this style if you like a minimal pendant that can work with different outfits or be layered with other necklaces. The [Aurora Singola Necklace](/products/iwjnk0004) is the collection’s solitaire example.

A circle-inspired pendant has a rounded outline that can feel balanced and continuous. Some designs use a solid disc; others have an open centre or combine the circle with additional diamond details. Check the actual design, since “circle pendant” can refer to different shapes.

The [Renata Necklace](/products/iwjnk0007) uses a ring-inspired circular form with a vertical diamond detail. It is a useful choice if you like a rounded shape but want more structure than a plain circle.
A star pendant has points radiating from a central area, creating a distinct outline. Depending on its proportions and setting, it can look delicate or more graphic.

The [Stella Necklace](/products/iwjnk0002) features a four-point star-inspired design with diamonds on its points and a solitaire diamond at the centre. Choose a star if you like celestial motifs or want the pendant’s outline to be easy to recognise.
A floral pendant uses a flower shape or an arrangement that resembles petals. The design may be formed from stones, metal or both, so check the close-up to see how the floral outline is made.
The [Fiorella Necklace](/products/iwjnk0008) has a floral diamond design. Consider it if you prefer a softer, nature-inspired silhouette over a straight or angular shape.

content.heading: Geometric pendants: defined lines and structure

content.text: Geometric pendants use clear shapes, lines or central arrangements. Some are symmetrical; others combine different forms for a more distinctive look. Their structured appearance can feel contemporary while remaining simple enough for regular wear.
The [Serafina Necklace](/products/iwjnk0012) has a geometric central arrangement. Choose a geometric style if you are drawn to defined shapes and a more architectural look.

content.heading: How to choose the right pendant shape

content.text: Start with the shape you already wear

Look at the jewellery you reach for most often. If you prefer simple pieces, a solitaire may fit your collection. If you like recognisable motifs, consider a star or floral pendant. If your accessories tend to have clean lines, look at geometric designs.
Think about how prominent you want the pendant to be

The outline affects how noticeable the pendant looks, but size, diamond placement, metal colour and chain length matter too. Compare the full necklace on a model or against a consistent background, not just the pendant close-up.
Consider the neckline

A short or high neckline may partly cover a pendant, while an open neckline can give its silhouette more space. The final position depends on the necklace length, pendant dimensions and clothing, so check the product measurements.
Decide whether you want one focal point or more detail

A solitaire puts emphasis on one centre stone. A floral or star design has more visual detail around its outline. A circle or geometric pendant can sit between those looks, depending on its construction.
Choose for repeat wear
Trends and occasions can help you discover a style, but choose a shape you will enjoy wearing beyond one event. If you are buying a gift, notice the motifs and shapes the recipient already wears.

faq.question: What are the main types of pendant shapes?
faq.answer: Common pendant shapes include solitaire, circle, star, floral, heart, geometric, drop and cluster designs. The shape describes the pendant’s visible outline or arrangement.

faq.question: What is the difference between a solitaire and a cluster pendant?
faq.answer: A solitaire pendant focuses on one centre stone. A cluster pendant groups multiple stones to form a larger design, such as a flower or another decorative shape.

faq.question: Are circle and geometric pendants the same?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. A circle pendant has a rounded outline. “Geometric” is a broader description for designs built around defined shapes or lines, which may include circles as well as squares, bars or other forms.

faq.question: Which pendant shape is best for everyday wear?
faq.answer: There is no single best shape. Choose one that suits your usual clothing and jewellery style, then check the product’s size, chain length and care information.

faq.question: How do I choose a pendant as a gift?
faq.answer: Look at the shapes, motifs and metal colours the recipient already wears. If you are unsure, a simple silhouette may be easier to coordinate, but check the chain length and product details before ordering.
